newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila's Congo plans road renaissance.
newsitem.headline: Kabila's Congo plans road renaissance.

text.p: Laurent Kabila's month-old government in the Democratic Republic of the Congo on Thursday announced plans to rebuild roads across the vast, rundown state.

"Five-hundred km (310 miles) of tarred road will be constructed in each province (of 11)," government spokesman Raphael Ghenda said on state television, after a cabinet meeting held on Tuesday and Wednesday in the eastern town of Kindu.
Ghenda reiterated earlier government promises that an estimated half a million civil servants would be paid this month, and set the date for payment as June 25.

He did not spell out how the government intends to finance its plans but said unspecified measures were being taken by the minister of finance to prevent the payment of salaries from causing an instant rise in inflation.

During three decades of corrupt rule under ousted dictator, Mobutu Sese Seko, successive governments frittered away revenues, ignoring investment in infrastructure and leaving civil servants unpaid for months on tiny salaries.
The number of usable roads in Congo is far less than it was at independence from Belgium in 1960.

Journeys around the interior can take weeks during bad weather, and transport costs are inflated -- with disastrous consequences for exports of agricultural products on which the mineral-rich country once depended.

Before Kabila's takeover a private foreign management team had restored regular train services in the south and east after years of stagnation. But Kabila scrapped the management contract in the name of nationalism, sending a tremor through business.
